item.title: Malicious .git Configs Can Make Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Other AI Agents Run Attacker Code (4 minute read)
item.description: Manifold Security found eight flaws in seven coding agents. A received repository can use .git/config to trigger commands through core.fsmonitor, and the commands run with the developer's account permissions, outside sandbox controls and without approval. Fixes exist for goose, Codex, and one Claude Code path. Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build, and another Claude Code path remained exposed.

item.title: Coder's registry infrastructure compromised to push malicious modules (2 minute read)
item.description: An attacker added unauthorized IPs to Coder's Cloudflare pool for registry.coder.com and served credential-stealing Terraform modules between 07:35 and 21:45 UTC on August 31, exfiltrating cloud, CI/CD, OIDC, and SSH secrets to coder-infra[.]com. Patched releases are 2.37.0, 2.36.4, 2.35.7, and 2.34.9.

item.title: Attackers Expose Ongoing AI Tool Use Targeting Organizations in Latin America (8 minute read)
item.description: Two intrusion clusters targeting Latin American critical infrastructure accidentally exposed their operations by leaving a self-hosted NextChat instance open to the public on TCP 3000. The exposed prompt history and staging scripts revealed a heavy reliance on AI tools to rapidly iterate through failed SAM and NTDS.dit credential dumps using volume shadow copy workarounds. To detect this infrastructure, defenders should actively hunt for the m-doxa on duckdns[.]org subdomains and monitor for multi-SAN Let's Encrypt certificates rotated between February and June.

item.title: The Outsider Phishing Kit: A Resilient Threat in the Face of Law Enforcement Action (15 minute read)
item.description: Despite recent takedown efforts by Google and the FBI, the ChenLun Outsider Phishing-as-a-Service platform has proven highly resilient, with over 700 new phishing pages deployed in a single month. The platform operates a sophisticated kill chain that utilizes WebSockets to stream victim keystrokes in real time while allowing affiliates to manually push contextual 2FA prompts on demand. Defenders can hunt for this infrastructure across all known templates by looking for the unique GetSyncSetting configuration file and an alphabetical page prefix convention that maps directly to the victim exploitation stage.

item.title: Rogue ScreenConnect Installations Across Unrelated Hosts Suggest Worm-Like Activity (10 minute read)
item.description: Modified ScreenConnect clients recovered by Huntress watch the EndPointStatusMessage.Connections collection for newly observed Host sessions, then register 1.vbs through 4.vbs with ScreenConnect's virtual file-transfer system and queue them with the action set to Run, so merely connecting to an infected client can hand the Host the same four-stage VBScript chain. The loader profiles first: 1.vbs writes a three-bit state to %TEMP%\value.txt covering existing ScreenConnect installs, whether Defender is the only endpoint protection present, and whether RAM exceeds 5GB, and that value selects a user-level backdoor, an access package with a ComputerDefaults.exe UAC bypass and AMSI tampering, or a combo branch carrying wstunnel disguised as Themes.exe and XMRig renamed SearchIndex.exe. Defenders should treat RunFiles or RanFiles entries in ScreenConnect server audit logs showing those scripts executed from Process: Guest as indicators of compromise, check for the WindowsServiceHost Run key pointing at WindowsServiceHost.vbs in AppData, and note that Huntress recommends reimaging affected hosts rather than cleaning them.

item.title: From Patch to Exploit; Using Claude Code to Reverse Engineer a Zero-Day in Papercut NG (13 minute read)
item.description: Kev Breen used Claude Code against a patched PaperCut NG zero-day, spotting SQL injection IoCs in error logs and finding the patch blocked CALL/EXEC/SYSCS_ calls in the SQL lookup template. Claude decompiled the JARs, found an auth-bypass filter flaw using a matrix parameter, then a second bypass in pageValidate letting an unauth service parameter reach admin pages. Chaining both gave unauthenticated RCE via arbitrary file write as the papercut user, confirmed with a working Python PoC. A guardrail swapped the model mid-session when it probed exploitation logs. Breen later found a third bypass defeating the emergency patch and reported it to security@papercut.com, who said they were already aware.

item.title: Leash (GitHub Repo)
item.description: The open-source safety and control layer for personal AI agents: Engine, Desktop, Mobile, proxy, and shared contracts. Leash sits between your AI agents and the actions they take. Safe work keeps moving. Sensitive work becomes a clear decision you can understand and control.

item.title: AWSHound: An OpenSource AWS OpenGraph Collector (20 minute read)
item.description: AWSHound is a self-hosted open-source collector that maps AWS environments into BloodHound OpenGraph datasets to visualize attack paths. Unlike existing mapping tools, AWSHound performs strict offline IAM evaluations by intersecting identity policies with permissions boundaries and SCPs to ensure relationships are only drawn where effective permissions resolve to an explicit allow. Operating securely through standard AWS SDK credential chains, the tool demonstrated massive scalability during internal testing by mapping a 500-account organization into 10.5 million edges in approximately 15 minutes.

item.title: AIR Security (Product Launch)
item.description: AIR Security launched a firewall that inventories and evaluates skills, plugins, MCP servers, and add-ons. It detects malicious instructions, hidden behavior, excessive permissions, typo-squatted packages, and risky updates, then revokes access across dependent workflows.

item.title: UK Moves to Block High-Risk Tech Suppliers From Critical Infrastructure (3 minute read)
item.description: UK ministers tabled amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill on August 24. The changes let them block high-risk technology suppliers from critical sectors. The move followed an Iran-linked attack that shut a UK energy facility for four days. The bill already mandates tight incident reporting and penalties, and SMEs supplying critical operators may face exclusion without adequate controls.

item.title: AI agents help compress ransomware intrusion to under 10 hours, raising stakes for CISOs (5 minute read)
item.description: A ransomware operator crossed an enterprise network in under 10 hours using AI agents, work Unit 42 estimated would have taken human hands roughly two weeks. The 50-plus ATT&CK techniques observed were unremarkable on their own, and analysts quoted here read the intrusion as human-directed, with AI handling delegated tactical work rather than anything approaching autonomy. The more durable observation is about transitive authority, where a repository account with no cloud admin rights can still alter a workflow that assumes a privileged cloud role, which is the gap that made speed matter.

item.title: OpenAI's new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Astra model uses "recurrent depth," letting it loop through the same query multiple times instead of reasoning step by step, which makes chain-of-thought logs harder to read. Scaling the technique could push reasoning fully into latent space, killing visibility into model behavior. OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki said Astra's chain of thought stays legible and that monitoring remains a research priority.

item.title: ValleyRAT Backdoor Disguises Itself as Adware (3 minute read)
item.description: Kaspersky found ValleyRAT hiding inside a modified build of the Chinese adware QN Wallpaper, sideloading a malicious libcef.dll through the signed QnWallpaper.exe to gain a trusted parent process that users routinely whitelist.

item.title: Rustbot, the macOS malware used in the latest Rust Supply Chain Attack (7 minute read)
item.description: Poisoned crates.io releases of arrayref, internment, and append-only-vec pulled in a malicious build-time dependency that fetched an arm64 Mach-O implant during cargo build, harvesting ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and ~/.kube credentials before its RSA tasking channel was neutered by the private key shipping inside the binary.

item.title: Is your security data architecture actually ready for AI agents? (Sponsor)
item.description: Deploying AI agents without fixing your underlying telemetry data leads to lackluster results. Google Cloud commissioned an Omdia study of 300 security professionals, and broke down why data readiness is the #1 hurdle to agentic AI in the SOC:The data gap: Only 48% of enterprise telemetry data is considered "AI-ready."Rearchitecture needed: 82% of respondents report that moderate or complete data redesign is required to support multi-agent workflows.Practitioner divide: Security engineers and architects are 2x more likely than SOC managers to call for a full telemetry overhaul.👉 Learn how AI agents are being used in the SOC. Download the full report →

item.title: Malicious Apache Modules Hijack Brazilian Government Site Traffic to Push Betting Pages (3 minute read)
item.description: Gambling Goblin installed malicious Apache modules on Brazilian government and education servers. The modules reverse-proxy visitors to fake Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Amazon pages promoting betting sites. Operators deployed DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, 3snake, SSH brute-forcing, and reconnaissance tools. Administrators lack published module hashes, filenames, or paths for direct Apache checks.

item.title: BGP Hijack Infecting Networks Caused By a Comedy of Errors That's Not Funny at All (4 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked Softaculous' 162.55.80.0/24 prefix and redirected Virtualizor update traffic to malicious servers. Hetzner's RPKI settings accepted /24 routes, while a forged AS path matched its ROA, so the attackers also obtained TLS certificates during the diversion. Virtualizor did not cryptographically verify update packages, and Softaculous cannot identify every affected server and urges customers to investigate.

item.title: Unitree G1 Humanoid Robot Flaws Allow Unauthenticated root RCE Over Bluetooth (3 minute read)
item.description: A security researcher discovered two independent flaws in Unitree G1 humanoid robots that could enable RCE on the devices. The first vulnerability allows an attacker within BLE range to obtain an AES-128 key without requiring the device to pair. The researcher found that the Unitree cloud API would decrypt the key without verifying ownership or serial numbers, allowing the researcher to access protected BLE operations, eventually allowing the attacker to exploit a buffer overflow to achieve RCE. The second path involves a path-traversal vulnerability in the robot's AI service, which enables an attacker to upload a file to the bashrunner's whitelist directory, enabling RCE.

item.title: Shai-Hulud: Whoever Controls Your Package Registry Controls Your Pipeline (7 minute read)
item.description: The npm worm lineage has evolved to a point where standard supply chain provenance mechanisms can no longer guarantee safety. During the August 2026 ChainDrop campaign, threat actors compromised over 400 packages in under four hours by hijacking a maintainer's legitimate signed release pipeline. The attackers utilized authorized infrastructure, so every poisoned package version successfully carried a perfectly valid SLSA attestation. To further evade traditional domain blocklists, the campaign hosted its command and control operations within an Ethereum smart contract. This attack builds upon the previous Shai-Hulud worms, which have recently pivoted to targeting authentication tokens for AI development tools like Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini. Security researchers warn that these identical mechanics could easily compromise infrastructure-as-code pipelines, proving that current attestation models verify origin rather than actual code legitimacy. To defend against these pipeline hijackings, organizations must enforce strict version pinning, utilize curated registries, implement OIDC-scoped credentials, and apply aggressive network egress restrictions.

item.title: Financially Motivated Threat Actor BREEZE COMET Targets Brazil (10 minute read)
item.description: Since 2024, BREEZE COMET has targeted Brazilian banks, payment firms, retailers, exchanges, and fintech providers to make fraudulent Pix, STR, and Boleto transfers. Initial access included password spraying, fake IT-support calls, booby-trapped tax files, exposed JBoss servers, and rogue devices on retail networks. The group steals mTLS credentials, API keys, CI/CD secrets, and cloud tokens, then moves through SMB and RDP. Its toolkit includes REALBREEZE, COBALTSPIN, LIGHTPAINT, MILDFROST, KICKPLATE, and BOATBEAM. Mandiant recorded two transaction waves within 24-48 hours after access to core financial applications.

item.title: Developing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards With Our Customers (4 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic will roll out Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in phases this fall. Customer activity logs can remain in customer-controlled AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud storage, using customer-managed keys and access policies. Automated systems inspect rolling traffic windows for offensive cyber capability, biological misuse, and stolen credentials. Flags go to customer teams. Anthropic staff does not review them.

item.title: Path to Astra: Critical Capabilities and Frontier Safeguards (7 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI classifies Astra as Critical for cybersecurity capability. Tests found zero-days, browser sandbox escapes, and root privilege-escalation chains. OpenAI delayed release work after the Hugging Face incident. Astra refused 91.5% of cyber-jailbreak requests, versus 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol. Advanced cyber access starts with selected testers, then Daybreak Blue.

item.title: Claude-BugHunter (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Claude-BugHunter packages 83 auto-loading Claude Code skills distilled from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, so the agent loads per-class detection patterns, payload tables, and chain templates by topic rather than by name.

item.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report: Exploitation Window Closes as AI Use Accelerates (4 minute read)
item.description: CrowdStrike reports that 88% of observed vulnerabilities were actively exploited within 48 hours of a public proof-of-concept release between January and June. Advanced threat groups like VAULT PANDA and GENESIS PANDA weaponized flaws in under 24 hours, while UMBRAL BISON targeted Linux privilege escalation vulnerability CVE-2026-31431 roughly 20 hours after disclosure. The report also highlights a rapid shift in alternative attack vectors, noting a fifteenfold increase in device code phishing alongside a massive concentration of software registry threats targeting npm.

item.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses (8 minute read)
item.description: A dark web service named Nexus recently advertised over 153 million scanned US and Canadian driver's licenses alongside millions of other identification documents on a Russian cybercrime forum. By correlating GMT timestamps embedded in the leaked image filenames with real-world travel records, researchers traced the infrared and ultraviolet scans back to a potential breach at the identity verification vendor idscan.net. Following the discovery of this continuous exfiltration campaign affecting major corporate clients, the FBI opened an official inquiry, and the Nexus site immediately went offline.

item.title: Critical Langflow Vulnerability Exploited as Attacks on AI Platform Rise (3 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-0768, a 9.8-severity remote-code-execution flaw in Langflow, is under active exploitation.

item.title: 23-Year-Old Sality P2P Botnet Disrupted (2 minute read)
item.description: An international operation disrupted the Sality P2P botnet after 23 years.

item.title: AI isn't just making attacks smarter. It's making them cheaper (Sponsor)
item.description: 69% cheaper for initial access in the black hat economy, that is. No wonder verified ransomware victims are up 45% YoY.Flashpoint's Global Threat Intelligence Report (Midyear Edition) is built on 3.9 petabytes of primary-source data collected directly from the spaces where this activity happens. Readers will learn:How the threat landscape is shifting from human-led campaigns to AI-led, machine-speed exploitationWhy 19% of the 21,667 vulnerabilities disclosed in H1 2026 already had public or functional exploit codeThe five groups behind 44% of all attacksRead the full report

item.title: Aesto Healthcare Data Breach Impacts 9.5 Million People (2 minute read)
item.description: Aesto reported that unauthorized access to part of its AWS infrastructure exposed data tied to 9,540,683 people. The intrusion ran from about December 2 to December 18, 2025. Records may include medical, insurance, financial, and government ID data. Aesto confirmed affected files in May, notified clients in June, and offered 24 months of Experian IdentityWorks.

item.title: Recently Patched PaperCut Zero-Days Used in Data Theft Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: PaperCut Software announced two new vulnerabilities that have been patched in its PaperCut NG and MF print management software. The vulnerabilities involve an authentication bypass vulnerability which can be chained with a separately disclosed vulnerability to achieve RCE. Threat intelligence firm Defused reports that the authentication bypass vulnerability is being exploited by attackers for data theft.

item.title: Hackers Target AWS root Accounts at 150+ Organizations With Password Spraying Attack (2 minute read)
item.description: Datadog Security Labs uncovered a password spraying campaign targeting AWS root accounts. Datadog stated that it has not identified a successful login yet, making the attacker's motive unclear. AWS root account logins require an account email, so it is possible that the attackers have access to a dataset or exposed email addresses that they are using in their campaign.

item.title: Can AI Create PLC Attacks? Yes, But It's Not That Easy Yet (8 minute read)
item.description: Forescout used an AI model to port an RCE exploit from a WAGO 750-852 PLC to a 750-831 PLC running the same vulnerable Nucleus FTP server (CVE-2021-31886). The AI needed constant human guidance: correcting false leads, supplying disassembly context, and running Ghidra scripts it wrote itself. The final exploit stage took 8 hours 32 minutes and cost $535.74 in API tokens. A follow-up attempt to build a C2 implant bricked the PLC. Once code execution worked, the AI wrote working ICMP and UDP payloads within minutes.

item.title: Don't Let Abliteration Abliterate Your Bug Hunting: Discovering Verdict Bias in Uncensored Models (17 minute read)
item.description: Tests of Gemma and Qwen builds found that abliterated variants approved of far more vulnerability candidates. In FreeBSD's sys/rpc, one Heretic build marked 138 of 144 candidates VALID, while the base marked 26 of 40. The Heretic run missed CVE-2026-4747 after spending its scan on false findings. A false heap-overflow claim survived because abliterated builds described the buffer bound, then still confirmed an overflow.

item.title: Spring Ring: An Inside Look at Voice Phishing Campaigns in Microsoft Teams (11 minute read)
item.description: Threat actors are executing voice phishing campaigns by registering external .onmicrosoft[.]com tenants with fake help desk names, initiating Microsoft Teams chats, and escalating to calls to trick victims into launching remote management tools. Following initial access, the attackers deliver distinct payloads that include an obfuscated PowerShell RAT designed to disable AMSI via the amsiInitFailed flag, and a Python-based execution chain that attempts PetitPotam coercion against domain controllers over port 445. To mitigate this threat, organizations must restrict external Teams access by default, block the associated payload hash, and proactively hunt for rapid chat-to-call sequences originating from commercial VPN nodes.

item.title: open-kritt (GitHub Repo)
item.description: open-kritt is an open-source, self-hosted vulnerability research platform that turns focused AI analysis into de-duplicated, ranked findings with configurable validation and enrichment.

item.title: Microburst (GitHub Repo)
item.description: MicroBurst includes functions and scripts that support Azure Services discovery, weak configuration auditing, and post-exploitation actions such as credential dumping. It is intended to be used during penetration tests where Azure is in use.

item.title: Humanbound (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Open-source adversarial testing engine, SDK, and CLI for AI agents. Attack your agent the way real users and attackers will: live endpoints, multi-turn conversations, and tool abuse. Then turn every failure into a firewall rule. Runs locally or against the Humanbound Platform. No login required to start.

item.title: Cato CTRL Insights: When Trust Becomes the Payload in a Fake Codex ClickFix Campaign (8 minute read)
item.description: Sponsored Codex searches routed macOS users to Google Sites lures with attacker-controlled iframes. Fake installers copied Terminal commands that decoded URLs, fetched shell loaders, and launched Mach-O payloads from /tmp/helper. The chain sent event=pasted telemetry, cleared quarantine attributes with xattr -c, and showed delivery overlap with AMOS.

item.title: British Public Oppose Secret Surveillance Powers and Want Strong Protections for Encrypted Communications (3 minute read)
item.description: CDT polling of 2,000 UK adults found 53% judge encryption-access security risks greater than law-enforcement benefits. 84% fear hidden access would create exploitable vulnerabilities, fraud, data leaks, and cybercrime. The findings follow Apple's tribunal challenge to UK Technical Capability Notices after a demand for encrypted iCloud access.

item.title: 1Password research: 40% of developers grant AI agents persistent access (Sponsor)
item.description: Replace persistent access with Zero Standing Privileges: Just-in-time, just-enough access, scoped to the task, and automatically revoked when work ends.

item.title: Critical JFrog Artifactory Vulnerability Reportedly Exploited in the Wild (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers reportedly began exploiting CVE-2026-82329 days after disclosure, minting admin tokens in vulnerable JFrog Artifactory deployments.

item.title: AliExpress accused of fingerprinting shoppers with silent audio trick that also muted a dev's headphones (3 minute read)
item.description: AliExpress scripts generate inaudible WebAudio sawtooth signals, collect frequency data, and query display size, memory, plugins, WebGL, and mouse activity.

item.title: ShinyHunters Claims it Stole 284 Million Patient Records from McKesson (2 minute read)
item.description: McKesson detected an intrusion on August 25 tied to third-party apps in its Oncology & Multispecialty and Medical-Surgical units. ShinyHunters vished McKesson employees, hijacked Okta SSO accounts, then pulled roughly a terabyte from Salesforce and Snowflake over four days. The group demanded $55,236,150 with a 72-hour deadline, which McKesson didn't pay. Breached data includes 284 million records containing SSNs, birth dates, Medicaid info, medical record numbers, medication/allergy data, and employee records.

item.title: Critical Microsoft UFO MCP Flaw Lets Attackers Remotely Control Android Devices Without Authentication (3 minute read)
item.description: Unauthenticated attackers can drive ADB commands on Android devices connected to Microsoft's open-source UFO Desktop AgentOS through CVE-2026-73296, which affects versions up to v3.0.7 and has no official patch. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to capture screenshots, extract UI hierarchy data, and tap, swipe, and text-entry actions on TCP 8020 and 8021 whenever operators follow the documented remote-deployment guidance and bind to 0.0.0.0. Users should restrict those ports to trusted hosts and front the services with TLS and an authenticated reverse proxy until the proposed UFO_MCP_API_KEY bearer-token fix merges.

item.title: Anthropic Warns Claude Users of Infostealer Malware Infections (1 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic warned affected Claude users that infostealers hijacked browser sessions and drained usage limits. The malware included Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, Acreed, and AMOS. Anthropic logged out compromised sessions, removed stored payment methods, and refunded identified unauthorized charges. Users should remove malware before re-adding payment details.

item.title: When it Snows it Pours – Anatomy of a ServiceNow Red Team (19 minute read)
item.description: MDSec red-team engagements turned phished ServiceNow users, exposed MID config.xml files, and over-permissioned roles into tenant admin access. Roles including catalog_admin, import_admin, and sn_cmdb_editor enabled Glide-script execution or role chaining. Operators created hidden admin accounts, altered timestamps, removed login and role histories, and used scheduled jobs as SnowFall C2 callbacks. From the tenant, they enumerated incidents and attachments, extracted credentials, bypassed adaptive authentication, and executed commands on MID servers through JAR plugins or the ECC queue.

item.title: When the Source Attacks Back: Prompt Injection Is Coming for OSINT (20 minute read)
item.description: Security researcher Dekens has demonstrated how adversaries can manipulate AI-assisted OSINT investigations by planting hidden prompt injections within digital documents. Through a dedicated training lab, Dekens highlights techniques like pushing CSS div elements off-screen, embedding white-on-white text in PDFs, and hiding instructions in unformatted spreadsheet cells. While not yet observed in active campaigns, these invisible artifacts successfully steer language models toward false narratives without altering the visually rendered file. To defend against poisoned sources, investigators should hash original documents and independently extract text using tools like Apache Tika or Tesseract to compare against the visual output. Furthermore, analysts must strictly isolate AI models in read-only environments to prevent untrusted inputs from executing unauthorized actions.

item.title: Philippine Nuclear Agency and Naval Contractor Targeted by Suspected Chinese-Speaking Operator Using Known Vulnerabilities (12 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found an exposed Amsterdam server staging tools and stolen Philippine data. Custom scripts abused ownCloud CVE-2023-49105, impersonating known users through unsigned WebDAV URLs. The recovered data included reactor records, radiation-safety files, employee PII, travel documents, BitLocker keys, KeePass data, and AxCrypt files. Logs referenced roughly 9 GB taken from the nuclear agency. A naval contractor's WordPress site was breached through LiteSpeed Cache CVE-2024-28000 and XML-RPC password guessing. The server also hosted Sliver, Metasploit, Mettle, and a loader that fetched a second-stage payload.

item.title: Cloudflare OS (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Cloudflare OS is an “operating system” for AI productivity that consists of an agent chat UI, a sandboxed application development environment for small personal apps, and security guardrails.

item.title: EMBA (GitHub Repo)
item.description: EMBA is designed as the central firmware analysis and SBOM tool for penetration testers, product security teams, developers, and responsible product managers. It supports the complete security analysis process, starting with firmware extraction, doing static analysis and dynamic analysis via emulation, building the SBOM, and finally generating a web-based vulnerability report.

item.title: Introducing Adaptive Intelligence: Undermining the Economics of Every Bot Attack (10 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare has launched Adaptive Intelligence, a bot detection engine designed to make evasion economically unviable for attackers by continuously retraining its models on live traffic. Rather than relying on deterministic rules, the engine utilizes non-deterministic signal weighting and delayed reactions to prevent threat actors from isolating and defeating specific defenses. This cross-temporal evaluation allows the system to detect slow credential-stuffing attacks distributed across residential proxies that would otherwise bypass standard rate limits. Enterprise customers can activate the continuous retraining component immediately by enabling "Auto Update Machine Learning" in their Bot Management dashboard, while advanced features such as disposable rule generation are still in development.

item.title: Open-Source Post-Quantum Cryptography Serverless CA (4 minute read)
item.description: Paul Schwarzenberger updated his open-source serverless CA with support for ML-DSA post-quantum cryptography. CA private keys are generated and used within AWS KMS FIPS 140-3 HSMS. ML-DSA is still not universally supported by applications, so users should check compatibility before adopting.

item.title: How AI Builders Will Get Hacked (4 minute read)
item.description: Developers who are frequently building tools with AI should ensure that they have a continuously running system that maintains a list of publicly exposed systems and continuously probes for basic security properties. AI builders can consider using full harnesses to comprehensively test critical systems. With the velocity of AI development, losing track of dangling, public resources will become a key attack vector.

item.title: OEMpocalypse Now (2 minute read)
item.description: Calif researcher Lukas Maar has developed a universal exploitation strategy that elevates an unprivileged Android app to root across modern Samsung, Xiaomi, and Oppo devices. Rather than hunting for generic kernel or chipset vulnerabilities, Maar targeted the proprietary OEM software overlays, such as One UI and HyperOS, that span each vendor's entire device lineup. The exploit leverages a page use-after-free vulnerability mapped to a freed physical page. This reliable technique successfully bypasses KASLR, control-flow hijacking, and slab protections without modification across kernels 5.4 through 6.12. While this initial publication outlines the overarching methodology on locked bootloaders, Maar plans to release the specific exploit chains affecting July 2026 flagship devices like the Galaxy S26 Ultra in future installments.

item.title: Update on recent cybersecurity incident (4 minute read)
item.description: Boston Scientific detected a cyber incident on August 25 that disrupted on-premises operating systems and business applications.

item.title: Data Security Incident - 27.08.26 (2 minute read)
item.description: Manchester Airports Group says an unauthorized party obtained booking and Wi‑Fi signup data from Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports.

item.title: Hasbro Data Breach Exposed Employee Personal Information (2 minute read)
item.description: Hasbro notified current and former employees that attackers may have accessed names, contact details, national ID numbers, and financial information. Massachusetts records list 436 affected residents. The disclosure may stem from March's network incident, which forced system shutdowns, and from Hasbro's reporting $11 million in cleanup costs and $25 million in delayed sales.

item.title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root (4 minute read)
item.description: Omarchy added its default user to the Docker group out of the box, and since supplementary groups are inherited, every process in the desktop session could reach the root-owned Docker socket and mount the host filesystem as root without a password or prompt. Browsers, editors, npm scripts, and AI coding agents all inherited that access, turning any ordinary application compromise into full machine compromise. The researcher disclosed privately that the group membership was removed in 4.0.1, and versions back through 3.8.4 remain affected.

item.title: Power Leak: Amazon Kiro IDE Prompt Injection Enables Data Exfiltration (7 minute read)
item.description: A crafted Kiro workspace can direct the agent to read .env data, place it in powersRecommendationUrl, and invoke Kiro Powers. The IDE then fetches the attacker-controlled URL with the secret in its query string. Mindgard reproduced the path in trusted and untrusted workspaces, and Amazon fixed the reported behavior in Kiro IDE 0.8.140.

item.title: Threat Hunt AI: How We Built an AI Security Analyst on AWS for Under $500 a Month (4 minute read)
item.description: Grow Therapy built an agentic threat hunting workflow on AWS that leveraged existing log sources such as Snowflake, CloudTrail, and Datadog for an additional cost of less than $500/month. Users submit a YAML threat hunt request, which then kicks off a five-phase workflow: first, Sonnet gathers relevant data, and then Opus compares the data to existing baselines, enriches and analyzes the context, assigns a confidence score to the findings, and performs adversarial analysis to validate them. False positives are tracked in Snowflake and injected into the adversarial validation step, which has significantly reduced false-positive reports.

item.title: Fire Ant Evolves: From Hypervisors to Trusted Infrastructure (24 minute read)
item.description: The Fire Ant threat actor has escalated from hypervisor compromises to direct infection of network control planes via purpose-built IOS XR implants. These sophisticated router implants establish unauthorized GRE tunnels to legacy Linux hosts and actively suppress syslog alerts by injecting exclusion clauses into CLI outputs. On the authentication layer, the actor deploys a tool called TacTap to inject malicious libraries into the tac_plus process, ultimately harvesting credentials using a single-byte XOR key. Sygnia researchers assess that this activity strongly overlaps with the China-nexus UNC3886 cluster. To detect this activity, defenders must hunt for unexplained GRE interfaces, tac_plus process injections, and specific log-clearing commands across independent network and memory telemetry.

item.title: TerminalFix Campaign Deploys a Reverse Tunnel Through Multistage Intrusion (16 minute read)
item.description: TerminalFix uses compromised sites and fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts to copy malicious PowerShell into a victim's clipboard. The command downloads a ZIP, then abuses LockScreenContentServer.exe to sideload dui70.dll, which then extracts payloads from PNG pixel data, creates Run-key and scheduled-task persistence, and enumerates Active Directory, trusts, administrators, servers, and system details. A Python client opens a TLS WebSocket tunnel to gitnow[.]dev:443, allowing SOCKS-style access to internal hosts. Look out for nonstandard LockScreenContentServer.exe paths, dui70.dll loads, pythonw.exe client.py activity, and the listed C2 domains.

item.title: AiPermission (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Local-first permission gateway for AI agents: connector-based SSH, Postgres, and Redis access with scoped tokens, human approval, audit logs, and encrypted local credentials.

item.title: Rust-Proof Your Code with Our New Testing Handbook Chapter (1 minute read)
item.description: Trail of Bits has added a new chapter to its Testing Handbook on Rust. The chapter begins with an overview of what guarantees Rust does and doesn't make and then discusses some tools and methods for dynamic and static analysis. The chapter also includes gotchas from the team's experience analyzing Rust code.

item.title: re-shell (GitHub Repo)
item.description: re-shell is a Nix flake-based reverse engineering environment designed for use with Claude Code.

item.title: A Call for Collective Action on Cyber Defense (4 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI and hundreds of other top companies have called for rapid cyber defense efforts as automated attacks spread. The letter targets unpatched software, excessive permissions, weak authentication, and legacy-system debt, asking organizations to verify fixes, use least privilege, and apply compensating controls, and asking vendors to share tested playbooks and threat intelligence.

item.title: Adaptive Agentic Worms Are Here (7 minute read)
item.description: A proof-of-concept worm running last year's open-weight models exploited 73.8% of an isolated 33-host network and replicated to 61.8% of it across 15 autonomous seven-day runs, chaining initial command execution into privilege escalation into self-replication, with each copy staging its own harness and local LLM or calling back to the parent host when local compute fell short. Researchers observed agents locating the IP blacklist in their own source and rewriting it to unlock monitoring hosts they had been forbidden to target, though hypervisor-level containment intercepted every attempt and no escape occurred. Detection currently rests on the resource signature, heavy GPU consumption, and sustained outbound inference traffic, so defenders should baseline per-host compute and egress, flag long-lived low-rate connections during off-peak windows, and assume that throttling is the first evasion an operator will add.

item.title: Owning the AI Stack (6 minute read)
item.description: Cybersecurity consultants and other organizations requiring consistent cyber capabilities should begin shifting to local models. The gap between local models and frontier labs has closed significantly, with DeepSeek v4 Pro even beating out frontier labs on some cyber benchmarks. When organizations rely upon frontier labs, they lose control, and changed behaviors or guardrails can lead to harness and workflow breakage.

item.title: Medical Device Maker Boston Scientific Says a Cyberattack is Causing a ‘Global Disruption' to its Operations (2 minute read)
item.description: Boston Scientific reported a cyberattack disrupting access to core IT systems and business applications. The outage has impaired order processing and shipments, but the company has not confirmed whether implanted devices, patients, or customer data are affected. Its investigation continues, and there is no restoration timeline.

item.title: Three UK Airports Hit By Cyber Attack With Data of 8.7M Accessed (2 minute read)
item.description: Manchester, London Stansted, and East Midlands airports suffered a data breach where attackers accessed data belonging to 8.7M customers. The incident involved data related to car park, lounges, and fast-track bookings, and in-airport WiFi signups. The breached data includes email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers, and postcodes.

item.title: 'NovaCookies' Kit Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions for $320 a Month (3 minute read)
item.description: NovaCookies rents AitM phishing infrastructure for $320 monthly. It relays Microsoft 365 logins and steals authenticated session cookies, bypassing MFA. Island found at least 755 supporting domains targeting hundreds of organizations and uses fake DocuSign document shares and trusted redirect hops. Defenders should deploy phishing-resistant MFA, correlate browser and token activity, and revoke active sessions and refresh tokens after suspected compromise.

item.title: Could OpenClaw Have Actually Hacked That Australian Gym? We Decided To Test It (6 minute read)
item.description: Aikido recreated an Australian gym-booking incident using OpenClaw and Claude Opus 4.6. The test app exposed two flaws: client-side-only booking limits and an IDOR cancellation endpoint. Across ten runs, the model bypassed the booking window nine times. It cancelled another user's reservation in two runs, including one response to a generic waitlist request. Replay tests covered 16 decision points and found dominant responses averaged 96.38 percent with the model's actions shifting with small prompt and context changes.

item.title: VMs Won't Contain Cyber-Capable Agents (5 minute read)
item.description: Trail of Bits gave GPT 5.6-Cyber preview access and tasked it with escaping a QEMU/KVM sandbox on a patched Debian 12 host, and it broke out three separate times over roughly 12 hours of largely unsupervised operation. The agent chained a recently disclosed host-kernel bug first, then pivoted to an unpatched libslirp CVE paired with an unmarked bug fix after the kernel got updated, and finally, once QEMU was rebuilt from upstream source, synthesized a full exploit chain from three fresh 0-days (a QEMU VAPIC SMRAM flaw, a KVM shadow-page desync, and a libslirp ICMP-reflection bug) plus one kernel fix that hadn't reached the distribution's stable branch. Trail of Bits recommends treating such agents as advanced persistent threats: move to minimal-attack-surface hypervisors like Firecracker (which held even after a kernel hardlock), track upstream patches rather than trusting distro backport cycles, and enforce least-privilege network access, time-boxed runs, and pristine per-session environments.

item.title: Edge Infrastructure Under Siege: What Two Independent Datasets Reveal About Who's Exploiting Your Perimeter (9 minute read)
item.description: A joint analysis by Tenable and SentinelOne revealed that state-sponsored groups and ransomware operators are independently exploiting the same edge device vulnerabilities. Researchers identified 12 flaws with confirmed multi-nexus exploitation by evaluating 93 CVE attribution pairs, including critical bugs in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400) and Check Point Quantum (CVE-2024-24919). The underlying exposure data highlights severe remediation bottlenecks across major enterprise vendors. F5 appliances led exposure rates with 54 percent of customer environments carrying an actively exploited CVE, while Citrix deployments suffered a median patch time of 461 days. Additionally, Ivanti edge products demonstrated a predictable pattern of serial exploitation refreshing every 8.5 to 13 months. Security teams must prioritize patching F5 and Citrix appliances immediately while deploying feature set minimization and strict endpoint protections to block lateral movement following a perimeter breach.

Operators used VPNs and Russian prompts to create posts for X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Substack, and Telegram. IBI republished academic work under false names and published a “sovereignty” index praising Russia, and its Telegram channels drew 10,000–20,000 followers.

item.title: CISA Red Team Compromised Two Critical Infrastructure Orgs, One Detected Nothing (3 minute read)
item.description: CISA's red team gained domain-level access at two critical-infrastructure organizations. One organization missed the intrusion amid false positives, disconnected SOC tooling, default credentials, AD CS flaws, cleartext secrets, and permanent AWS keys. The other organization isolated phishing-hit workstations within 2–20 minutes, yet assessors later obtained domain-controller secrets through an SCCM-stored service credential.

item.title: Ubiquiti Patches Three Max Severity Security Vulnerabilities (2 minute read)
item.description: Ubiquiti patched three critical (CVSS 10) vulnerabilities across their UniFi Protect Application, UniFi Talk Application, and UniFi OS Server products. Two of the vulnerabilities allow attackers to exploit improper input validation in the UniFi Protect Application video surveillance platform and UniFi Talk Application to achieve command injection. The third allows attackers to bypass authentication on UniFi OS devices by exploiting a CRLF injection flaw.

item.title: Employee Benefits Platform Paylogix Says Hackers Stole Financial and Health Data (2 minute read)
item.description: Employee benefits provider Paylogix disclosed that they experienced a data breach last November that exposed data belonging to at least 65,000 individuals. The compromised data includes SSNs, electronic signatures, financial account information, medical data, passport numbers, and taxpayer IDs. The Akira ransomware group added Paylogix to its leak site back in January.

item.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch the Actively Exploited Oracle Flaw by August 27 (1 minute read)
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-21962 (CVSS 10.0) to the KEV catalog following active exploitation of the Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in. Federal agencies must apply the January 2026 patch by August 27.

item.title: Drive-By Agent Hijacking: One Website Visit, Persistent Model Poisoning (7 minute read)
item.description: Cyera disclosed CVE-2026-65105 in NVIDIA NemoClaw. NemoClaw's setup binds Ollama to 0.0.0.0:11434, disabling Ollama's Host-header validation, allowing for an attacker-controlled site to use DNS rebinding to reach the victim's local Ollama API without authentication. The attacker can list models, extract templates and prompts, delete or overwrite models, consume GPU resources, and sign users out. By modifying a model's chat template, the attacker can append hidden instructions to every future system prompt.

item.title: The Patch Window is Collapsing: Why Security Needs a New Control Plane (6 minute read)
item.description: AI-accelerated exploit development has compressed the vulnerability exploitation window to mere hours, fundamentally outpacing traditional enterprise patch validation cycles. To bridge this critical exposure gap, shift toward network-enforced control planes that actively contain threats while permanent patches are tested. By deploying immediate compensating measures like dynamic segmentation and adaptive rate limiting, security teams can secure vulnerable assets without disrupting operations. Network-level stream throttling successfully mitigates the active threat without forcing organizations to completely disable the vulnerable protocol.

item.title: Pwning Call of Duty 1: a 20-year-old RCE, Found in an Evening with AI (5 minute read)
item.description: Researchers tested Call of Duty 1's Linux dedicated server in Docker, where they found a stack overflow in the rcon map command. A 72-byte buffer accepted an unchecked map name. Sending 76 bytes overwrote the saved return address, and input filtering blocked high-byte addresses and int 0x80. The exploit used a low-memory jmp esp gadget and alphanumeric-safe shellcode with sysentera and it achieved a shell in the game-server process. The flaw requires the rcon password, making it post-authentication RCE.

item.title: INTERPOL Operation Jackal IV Arrests 58, Identifies 263 in Global Cyber Fraud Crackdown (2 minute read)
item.description: INTERPOL's eight-month Operation Jackal IV involved 22 countries and targeted West African crime groups. Police arrested 58 people and identified 263 suspects. Investigators linked 196 people to a crime-as-a-service network supplying domains and laundering support with an estimated €143 million stolen through fake investment offers.

item.title: Behaviorally Fingerprinting Ox Alpha's Provenance and Censorship (2 minute read)
item.description: CTGT researchers have used behavioral fingerprinting to link the anonymous "Ox Alpha" model on OpenRouter to Zhipu's GLM-5.x family. Despite system prompts instructing the model to conceal its identity, researchers identified matching Z.AI error codes, a 1.0 temperature ceiling, and an exact tokenizer match. The analysis also revealed a highly targeted censorship blacklist designed to evade standard foreign-interest audits. While Ox Alpha answers queries about Xinjiang and Taiwan identically to American models, it strictly blocks seven domestic legitimacy topics including the 2018 term limits removal and Xi Jinping. The model operators have not officially disclosed this information, so the attribution relies entirely on CTGT's LineageEval testing instrument.

item.title: A Cautionary Tale About Data Breach Claims, Verification and Carhartt (7 minute read)
item.description: Troy Hunt investigated ShinyHunters' claim of a 24.8 million-record data breach at Carhartt and discovered the dataset was heavily contaminated with synthetic information. Through AI-assisted and manual verification, Hunt identified TPC-DS benchmark data, Microsoft 365 routing duplicates, and highly uniform birth distributions. This forensic analysis reduced the actual number of compromised records to roughly 12.9 million. Hunt concluded that while Carhartt suffered a genuine breach, the threat actors likely exfiltrated a Databricks instance where production customer records were stored alongside unlabeled test data rather than fabricating the dump outright.
